grammars.title: The subject pronoun on

teach.title: On = people, you, they
teach.body: On means people in general: “you”, “they”, “people”, “one”. It always takes the il / elle form of the verb: on fait, on va, on aime.

examples.fr: En France, on fait les courses tous les jours.
examples.en: In France, people shop every day.
examples.pr: ahn FRAHNSS, ohn FEH lay KOORSS too lay ZHOOR
examples.fa: آن فرانس، اُن فِ لِ کورس تو لِ ژور

examples.fr: En France, on ne trouve pas de médicaments au supermarché.
examples.en: In France, you don't find medicine at the supermarket.
examples.pr: ahn FRAHNSS, ohn nuh troov PAH duh may-dee-kah-MAHN oh sü-pehr-mar-SHAY
examples.fa: آن فرانس، اُن نُ تروو پا دُ مِدیکامان اُ سوپِرمارشه

teach.trick: On always takes the il form: on fait, never on faisons.

teach.title: On = we (everyday French)
teach.body: In conversation, French speakers usually say on instead of nous. The verb still takes the il form.

examples.fr: Vous rentrez à quelle heure, Monique et toi ?
examples.en: What time are you and Monique coming home?
examples.pr: voo rahn-TRAY ah kel UHR, moh-NEEK ay TWAH
examples.fa: وو رانتره آ کِل اُر، مُنیک اِ توآ

examples.fr: On rentre tard, après le film.
examples.en: We'll be home late, after the movie.
examples.pr: ohn RAHN-truh TAR, ah-PREH luh FEELM
examples.fa: اُن رانتر تار، آپرِ لُ فیلم

examples.fr: Albert et moi, on aime le cinéma.
examples.en: Albert and I like the movies.
examples.pr: al-BEHR ay MWAH, ohn-NEM luh see-nay-MAH
examples.fa: آلبِر اِ موا، اُنِم لُ سینِما

teach.trick: Nous allons = on va. Same meaning, but on is what you'll hear on the street.

teach.title: Hear the n
teach.body: The n of on is silent before a consonant: on fait (“ohn FEH”). Before a vowel it links: on_achète (“ohn-nah-SHET”), on_aime (“ohn-NEM”).
teach.trick: Vowel after on? Link the n, like nous_aimons.

notes: On = people, you, they, one (general statements).
On = nous in everyday speech: On y va ! = Let's go!
On always takes the il / elle verb form: on fait, on va, on aime.
The n links before a vowel: on_achète, on_aime.

tricks.on: On + il form: on fait, on va, on mange.
tricks.nous: Casual we = on: Albert et moi, on aime le cinéma.

drills.text: En France, on ___ les courses tous les jours.
drills.en: In France, people shop every day.
drills.why: On takes the il form: fait.

drills.text: Albert et moi, on ___ le cinéma.
drills.en: Albert and I like the movies.
drills.why: On = we, but the verb takes the il form.

drills.text: Nous allons au café. = ___ au café.
drills.why: On + il form of aller: va.

drills.text: Say it in French: We're coming home late. (use on)

drills.why: Before a vowel, the n of on links.

drills.text: Say it in French: In Canada, people speak English and French.
drills.answer: Au Canada, on parle anglais et français.
accept: Au Canada, on parle anglais et français.
Au Canada, on parle français et anglais.

exercisesIntro.title: Exercices du manuel
exercisesIntro.body: Exercice 7 (p. 100): a curious French person asks about life in the United States. Your real answer can be oui or non; here you practise the forms with on.

exercises.text: Aux États-Unis, est-ce qu'on regarde beaucoup la télévision ? — Oui, on ___ beaucoup la télévision.
exercises.en: Do people watch a lot of TV in the US? Yes, people watch a lot of TV.

exercises.text: Est-ce qu'on mange toujours des hamburgers ? — Non, on ne ___ pas toujours des hamburgers.
exercises.en: Do people always eat hamburgers? No, they don't always eat hamburgers.

exercises.text: Est-ce qu'on va au restaurant tous les jours ? — Non, on ne ___ pas au restaurant tous les jours.
exercises.en: Do people go to restaurants every day? No.

exercises.text: Est-ce qu'on dine à huit heures du soir ? — Non, on ne ___ pas à huit heures du soir.
exercises.en: Do people eat dinner at 8 p.m.? No.

exercises.text: Est-ce qu'on aime les films français ? — Oui, on ___ les films français.
exercises.en: Do people like French films? Yes.

exercises.text: Est-ce qu'on fait des promenades en famille le dimanche après-midi ? — Oui, on ___ des promenades en famille.
exercises.en: Do families go for walks on Sunday afternoons? Yes.

exercises.text: Est-ce qu'on aime parler de la politique ? — Non, on n'___ pas parler de la politique.
exercises.en: Do people like to talk about politics? No.

exercises.text: Est-ce qu'on étudie beaucoup la géographie ? — Non, on n'___ pas beaucoup la géographie.
exercises.en: Do people study geography a lot? No.
